Full layouts of boot parameter block, BIOS register block, disk info and parameter structures, descriptor pointer, task registers and port operation tables beyond referenced fields.

Behavior of BIOS invocation helpers, segment and stack queries, pointer helpers, build assertions, default I O setup, console, CPU validation, power query, video setup, gate enable, loader messaging and halting.
Heap pointer units, setup move size, code entry address, real mode switch block format, heap end pointer base and command line buffer handling beyond cited branches.

Die lock type and initial state, oops context entry and exit, spinlock bustle, crash kernel check and invocation, taint flags, panic flags and behavior, interrupt context test and task stack unpoisoning.
Task death routine, per CPU stack top, stack padding and register frame sizes, frame pointer clearing effects and unwinder hints.
Register display mode enumerations, log level strings, MSR identifiers, debug register reset values, CPU feature test, carry flag test, protection key enable test and kernel no fault copy semantics.
Command line option parsing defaults for disk, quiet and debug, build configuration defaults for power, disk and isolation features, and video and memory table capacities.

findings.text: Early serial defaults treat COM1 base as 0x3f8 and default speed as 9600 baud, with base baud defined as 1843200 divided by 16.

UART register offsets relative to base place transmit and receive and low divisor at 0, interrupt enable and high divisor at 1, interrupt identity and FIFO control at 2, line control at 3, modem control at 4, line status at 5, modem status at 6, with divisor latch access bit valued 0x80.

Port I O abstraction is a structure holding three callables: one reading a byte from a 16 bit port, one writing a byte to a 16 bit port, and one writing a 16 bit word to a 16 bit port. Short names map to the corresponding members of the global instance.
Boot stage exposes a 16 byte aligned global boot parameter block, a global port operations instance, and two heap cursors both starting at end of image with default meaning no heap.

Boot header copy requires parameter block size 4096, copies header from setup header, and when new style command line pointer is absent but old magic matches, synthesizes pointer from old offset plus segment, choosing current data segment when offset lies below setup move size and 0x9000 otherwise.

Heap initialization applies only when load flags advertise heap, sets heap end from header heap end pointer plus 512, clamps it to below current stack minus reserved stack size, and otherwise warns about ancient loader with limited function.

Main setup routine is the high level boot orchestrator that prepares I O, parameters, console, heap, CPU validation, BIOS mode, memory, keyboard, speed step, power and disk queries, video, then protected mode transfer.

Setup order is default I O then header copy then console then optional debug notice then heap then CPU check with fatal message on failure then BIOS mode hint then memory detection then keyboard then speed step then conditional power management then conditional disk data then video then protected mode with no return.
Keyboard setup queries lock flags through BIOS keyboard service and stores low result in boot parameters, then requests a fixed repeat configuration.
Speed step query is skipped on CPU level below 6, otherwise issues BIOS extended service with fixed request signature and stores returned signature command event and level into boot parameters.
64 bit BIOS mode hint issues BIOS service with fixed function and mode selector and no result handling.
Memory detection entry runs three probes in fixed order: extended address map, then E801, then 88h.

Extended map probe repeatedly invokes BIOS map service starting with zero continuation and fixed signature, threading continuation across calls, using a zeroed static staging entry copied to table, breaking on carry, discarding all results on signature mismatch including mid loop loss, and stopping on zero continuation or table full before recording count.

E801 probe ignores failures signaled by carry, prefers extended registers when either is nonzero, rejects sizes above 15 times 1024 as bogus, encodes exact 15 MB case as shifted extended value plus base, and otherwise records low size as alternate kilobytes.
88h probe unconditionally records returned register as extended kilobytes in screen info.
Disk query is the BIOS disk probing entry that honors command line control and quiet flag before scanning BIOS hard disks.

Disk probing parses edd option with skip and skipmbr enabling extended data without signature, off disabling all, on forcing enable, respects build default and quiet, then iterates BIOS units from 0x80 upward, appending successful extended records while table has room and separately advancing signature buffer while counting consecutive signature successes.

Extended disk record collection first probes extension presence with fixed magic and rejects on carry or mismatched reply magic, stores unit version and feature flags, requests device parameters with length preset, then requests legacy geometry with cleared segment and decodes cylinder head and sector fields only on success.

Legacy sector read requests one sector at cylinder head sector start through disk service and maps carry to zero or minus one. Signature collection chooses sector size defaulting to 512, builds naturally aligned heap buffer after end of image, requires heap flag and room below heap limit, zeroes buffer, reads sector, extracts 32 bit signature and validates trailing magic against 0xAA55.
Protected mode transfer is the boot entry that leaves real mode after preparing gates, masks and tables.

Protected mode sequence runs real mode hook, gate enable with fatal message on failure, coprocessor reset, interrupt masking, null descriptor table load, global descriptor load, then 32 bit jump with kernel entry and physical parameter address.
Real mode exit hook either far calls loader supplied switch address or otherwise disables interrupts and masks nonmaskable interrupt through CMOS port with delay.
Pre transition masking fully masks secondary controller and masks primary except cascade, each followed by delay. Coprocessor reset writes zero to two fixed ports each followed by delay.

Boot descriptor tables use a 16 byte aligned three entry table for 32 bit code and data covering 4 GB at base zero plus a 104 byte task segment at base 4096 kept only for virtualization, loaded with computed physical address and kept static for hypervisor pointer bug, while interrupt table is loaded as null zero base and limit.
Low level protected jump is the assembly entry that completes the mode switch to 32 bit code.

Low level jump preserves parameter pointer in preserved register, fixes up forward target by current code segment base, serializes with short jump, preloads data and task selectors, sets protection enable in control register, then far jumps to 32 bit entry with boot code selector.
Fatal exception entry wraps detailed reporting between oops begin and end, defaulting to segmentation signal unless reporting indicates suppression.

Oops begin enters oops context, saves interrupt state without deadlock guarantee, records current CPU, acquires global die lock with try then blocking path distinguishing nested same CPU case, increments nesting, records owner, enables verbose console and releases spinlock bustle.

Oops end optionally triggers crash kernel, clears spinlock bustle, clears owner, taints, decrements nesting and releases die lock only at zero, restores interrupts, exits oops context, prints executive summary from saved registers, returns on zero signal, otherwise panics in interrupt or when configured, else unpoisons task stack and rewinds to kill task.

First oops saves registers for later summary, then emits header with message truncated error code incremented counter and build and runtime flags for SMP page alloc kasan and page table isolation. Detailed path runs header then body and returns body result.
32 bit and 64 bit fatal unwind entries clear frame pointer, switch to per CPU top of stack minus register and padding area, invoke task death routine, with 32 bit form looping forever after call.

Opcode capture copies a window starting 42 bytes before instruction pointer totaling 64 bytes, using kernel no fault copy in kernel mode, rejecting other tasks user code with permission error, otherwise using non faulting user copy safe in any context, then prints marked byte window or permission silence or access failure message.

Instruction pointer display prints segment qualified symbol plus opcode dump, with 32 bit and 64 bit address formatting variants, while interrupt return display appends stack segment pointer and flags on same line.

32 bit register dump prints general registers then segment selectors with current GS and flags, returns early unless full mode, otherwise adds control registers and debug registers only when outside reset defaults.

64 bit register dump starts with interrupt return registers and original accumulator, prints all general registers, supports short return, user mode base dump, and full mode with selectors, FS GS and kernel GS bases, control registers, conditional debug registers and conditional protection key when enabled.

Boot services use disk interrupt 0x13, keyboard 0x16, system 0x15, with functions for legacy read, extension check, device parameters, legacy geometry, map, E801, 88h, speed step and mode hint; transition uses CMOS 0x70 with disable value 0x80, PIC ports 0x21 and 0xA1, coprocessor ports 0xF0 and 0xF1, MBR magic 0xAA55, and sector 0-0-1 start.

Signature probing fails safely without heap flag or room, avoiding overflow past heap limit, while disk scan warns that faulty BIOS may hang and offers disable option, and extended map treats mid scan signature loss as total failure rather than partial map.

Transition hazards include unaligned global table known to fail boot hence 16 byte alignment, hypervisor storing pointer to descriptor pointer requiring static storage, null interrupt table invalidating interrupts during switch, and gate failure being fatal.

Oops path hazards include racy interrupt save preferring liveness over strict safety, nested oops on same CPU tolerated without deadlock, and fatal handling avoiding return on tiny or special stacks by rewinding before killing task.

Boot and diagnostic interface exposes memory detection, disk query, protected mode transfer, low level jump, fatal reporting with begin and end, instruction and register display, opcode display and detailed die helpers.
Boot I O header defines an inclusion guard, while string conversion helper forwards variadic arguments to single expansion stage.

Diagnostic display entries provide instruction pointer with opcodes, interrupt return registers, full and short register dumps on both widths, and detailed die reporting bracketed by oops begin and end.
